text:
# SEO and GEO audit: acme-mugs The repo is a small Vite + React single-page app with two routes. It is client-rendered only, so crawlers and AI bots get almost nothing useful. The problems are below, most severe first. ## Critical **1. `public/robots.txt:1-2` blocks every crawler from the whole site.** `User-agent: *` with `Disallow: /` stops Google, Bing, GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot and all other bots from indexing or citing anything. - Fix: replace it with the following (and add a `Sitemap:` line once the sitemap exists, see #6): ``` User-agent: * Allow: / Sitemap: https:///sitemap.xml ``` - If you want to block specific AI training bots, add per-bot `Disallow` rules instead of a blanket block. **2. The site is client-side rendered only (`index.html:8`, `src/main.jsx:16`).** The served HTML is an empty `
`. Many AI crawlers don't run JavaScript. Google renders JS, but later and less reliably. As served, the site has no content, headings or links for most bots. - Fix: pre-render or server-render the pages. Options are an SSR/SSG framework (Next.js, React Router framework mode, Astro), or `vite-plugin-ssr`/`vike`, or a prerender step for `/` and `/catalogue`. **3. The catalogue content is fetched after load (`src/pages/Catalogue.jsx:5-7`, rendered at line 11).** Product names only appear after a client-side `fetch('/api/mugs')`. Crawlers that don't execute JS see an empty catalogue, and even Google may miss it. - Fix: load the data at build or server time (SSG/SSR loader) so the product list is in the initial HTML. - The `.then(setItems)` has no error handling, and the response isn't checked with `r.ok`. ## High **4. Placeholder title and no meta description (`index.html:5`, `index.html:4`).** The title is "Vite App" on every page, and there is no ``. - Fix: add a unique title and description per route, for example "Handmade Ceramic Mugs from Bristol | Acme Mugs". Use `react-helmet-async`, React 19's native ``/`<meta>` hoisting, or your SSR framework's metadata API. **5. Missing `lang` and viewport (`index.html:2`, `index.html:3-6`).** - Add `<html lang="en">`. - Add `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />`. Without it, mobile-friendliness suffers. **6. No sitemap, canonical URLs or social tags.** None of these exist anywhere in the repo. - Add `public/sitemap.xml` (or generate it at build time) listing `/` and `/catalogue`, plus one URL per mug once product pages exist. - Add `<link rel="canonical">` per page. - Add Open Graph and Twitter tags (`og:title`, `og:description`, `og:image`, `og:url`) for link previews. **7. Product items have no URLs (`src/pages/Catalogue.jsx:11`).** Each mug is a plain `<p>` with only a name. There are no detail pages and no links, so nothing is indexable per product and AI engines can't cite a specific mug. - Fix: add a route such as `/catalogue/:slug`, link to it with `<Link>` from the catalogue, and render a name, description, price and image on each product page. ## Medium **8. Navigation uses a button instead of a link (`src/main.jsx:11`).** `<button onClick={() => navigate('/catalogue')}>` has no `href`, so crawlers can't follow it and the catalogue is unreachable by link. It's also worse for accessibility. - Fix: use `<Link to="/catalogue">Catalogue</Link>` as on line 10, and drop the unused `useNavigate` import. **9. The hero image has no alt text, dimensions or lazy-load strategy (`src/pages/Home.jsx:5`).** `<img src="/hero.jpg" />` gives no alt text for image search or AI descriptions, and no `width`/`height`, which causes layout shift (CLS). - Fix: `<img src="/hero.jpg" alt="Handmade ceramic mug on a wooden table" width="1200" height="800" fetchpriority="high" />`. - Also consider serving WebP or AVIF. `public/hero.jpg` is also not tracked in the repo, so confirm it exists. **10. No structured data anywhere (GEO).** Add JSON-LD so search and AI engines can read the business and products reliably: - `Organization` or `LocalBusiness` (Bristol, UK) on the home page. - `Product` with `offers` (price, currency, availability) for each mug. - `BreadcrumbList` on the catalogue and product pages. ## Lower priority (GEO content) **11. Thin copy (`src/pages/Home.jsx:4-6`).** The whole home page is one H1 and one sentence. For AI answer engines to cite you, add: - Concrete facts: materials, clay and glaze types, dishwasher and microwave safety, sizes and capacity, shipping regions and times, and price range. - An FAQ section, which also fits `FAQPage` markup. - An About section covering who makes the mugs and where. **12. The catalogue heading is generic (`src/pages/Catalogue.jsx:10`).** "Catalogue" says nothing about the content. Use something like "Handmade Ceramic Mug Collection", and add an intro paragraph. **13. Missing `llms.txt`.** This is optional and its impact is unproven. A short `public/llms.txt` summarising the site and linking to key pages is cheap to add. **14. Missing semantic landmarks.** `<nav>` and `<main>` are present, which is good. Add a `<header>` and `<footer>` (with contact details and a business address), and avoid heading-level gaps as pages grow. ## Suggested order 1. Fix `robots.txt` (#1), a one-line change. 2. Move to SSR or prerendering (#2, #3), since everything else depends on it. 3. Add titles, descriptions, `lang` and viewport (#4, #5) and a link-based nav (#8). 4. Add product pages, the sitemap and structured data (#6, #7, #10). 5. Add image alt text and expand the copy (#9, #11, #12). I haven't changed anything. Tell me if you'd like me to apply the quick fixes (#1, #4, #5, #8, #9), which are small and low-risk.
